name: TX-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -13 point partisan lean
Steinmann's large fundraising and outside support versus Jones's minimal resources
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 94%
Open seat removes incumbent-specific risk but no polling is available
model.rationale: The district's -13 Republican lean, the Democrat's negligible fundraising, and markets pricing the GOP near 94% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings to shift the picture, the fundamentals-based margin of about -15 stands.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected spending surge by the Democrat would be the first sign the race is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-08 is an open Republican-held seat north of Houston, with Morgan Luttrell retiring. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann enters as the clear favorite in a district that leaned about 13 points Republican in recent presidential voting. She has raised roughly $2.4 million and drawn about $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised only about $31,000 with no outside spending on either side.

Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 94%, and no expert raters or general-election polls are available for this race. The forecast rests on the district's partisan lean and the stark resource gap, pointing to a Republican win in the mid-teens with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
